extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, and patent examiners interacting with the Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO)
extracted.subtask_description: KIPO examination guideline excerpts setting eligibility, required documents, prior-art-search report content, amendment/notification rules for expedited examination, and rules for examiner reconsideration prior to appeal for Korean patent (and utility model) applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written explanation on correspondence (mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: An explanation on correspondence must be submitted in any case; any differences shall be indicated in a written explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike any other evidential documents, an explanation on correspondence must be submitted in any case. Where 'opinions on an international application' are indicated in foreign written opinions or reports, the intention that all claims of the concerned patent application are not affected by those opinions shall be explained. Explanations may include i) responses to the opinions and ii) claims that irregularities are addressed through amendments. Where such explanations are not indicated, an examiner may order to amend the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification rule for determination of expedited examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination on expedited examination is not notified to a requester except where the request is rejected; a rejection must be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining expedited examination agreed with a foreign patent office, the result shall not be notified to the requester; however, if the request is rejected, it shall be notified like other rejected requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redetermination when applicant amends after expedited determination
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant amends claims after a determination on expedited examination so that claims differ from prior explanations/foreign-recognized claims/international search conclusions, examiner may instruct corrections and re-determine eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant amended a specification with claims not included in the explanation on comparison with prior art, or claims not substantially identical with claims a foreign patent recognizes to be patentable, or claims not substantially identical with claims decided to meet novelty/inventive step/industrial applicability in international search/examination, the examiner may instruct corrections for the expedited-exam request and re-determine whether to permit expedited examination. Examiner may grant a correction order designating a period up to one month at his discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited examination without redetermination when full correspondence provided
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant submits a comparison explanation covering all claims (including amended ones) against prior art cited by a foreign office, or correspondence with claims recognized patentable by a foreign office, or claims meeting requirements in international search/examination, expedited examination shall proceed without redetermination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicant submits explanation on comparison between all claims (including amended) and prior art cited in foreign examination notifications; or correspondence with claims recognized to be patentable by a foreign office; or correspondence with claims meeting novelty/inventive step/industrial applicability in international search/examination, expedited examination shall be conducted without undertaking re-determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model expedited-examination eligibility (filed & requested within two months)
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility model application requested for examination upon filing and then requested for expedited examination within two months from filing is eligible for expedited examination; patent application is not eligible under this provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: utility models have a 10-year term and typically shorter life-cycles. Note: a utility model application divided or converted from a prior-filed application cannot hold the retrospective filing date of the prior application and divisional/converted utility model applications cannot be requested for expedited examination based on these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility of divisional/converted utility model for expedited exam
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional or converted utility model application cannot claim the retrospective filing date of the prior-filed application and therefore cannot be requested for expedited examination under this rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such applications are not eligible for expedited examination even if initial filing/requests would otherwise suggest eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for specialization-project-related patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application directly related to a specialization project under the specified Act is eligible for expedited examination; utility model applications are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic requirements: (i) where jointly filed, one applicant must be recognized by heads of central administrative agencies as a specialization project operator or participant; (ii) applicant must be designated as operator/participant on at least one of filing date, request date, or determination date; (iii) determination can be evidenced by official gazette; (iv) invention must be directly related to the specialization project as determined from the written explanation and the official gazette (and relevant websites). Examiner may order correction if correlation not recognized; if likely related without special grounds, examiner may recognize eligibility without further investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for medical-services-R&D patent applications in high-tech complexes
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications directly related to R&D of medical services within designated high-tech medical complexes, filed by resident R&D medical institutes, are eligible for expedited examination; utility model applications are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic requirements: (i) in joint filings at least one applicant must be a resident R&D institute of medical services under the Special Act; (ii) designation must be effective on at least one of filing/request/determination dates; (iii) inventions must be directly related to R&D of the concerned medical service. Examiner may order corrections to verify correlation, but may accept eligibility if relation is likely and no special grounds exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art search by authorized institute required for certain expedited requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester shall commission prior art search of the claimed invention to one of the authorized prior art search institutes designated by the Commissioner (listed institutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized institutes include specified organizations (e.g., Korea Institute of Patent Information, WIPS, IP Solutions). The authorized institute must submit Search results under Annexed Form no. 4 within one month after the request for expedited examination. Failure to submit within one month triggers a correction order; the correction order is sent to both the requester and the institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination based on authorized prior-art search report
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a prior-art search report is submitted by an authorized institute, the examiner shall make a determination on expedited examination; identical claims between the application and the search report support recognition of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the authorized institute fails to meet the guideline for writing the report and the report cannot be used, the examiner shall issue a correction order within the designated period and may reject the expedited-exam request if the search report is not corrected. A written explanation for the request must be attached unless the application is marked as having requested prior-art search and the written request includes institute name and date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written request / marking when prior-art search commissioned
rubrics_metrics.description: If prior-art search is requested to an authorized institute and the request for expedited examination includes the institute name and date, no additional written request is needed; the application shall be marked accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the application is marked as requested for prior-art search and the written request includes the information on the authorized institute and date of request, the ground for the expedited-exam request is clearly explained and an additional written request does not need to be attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of parent prior-art search report for divisional expedited requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If expedited examination was determined for the parent based on authorized prior-art search reports and all claims of a divisional were already examined in that parent report, a request for expedited examination on the divisional can be filed without additional prior-art search, subject to showing claims identity and inclusion in the parent's search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should submit a contrastive explanation indicating claims of divisional are identical to parent claims and a written explanation that the divisional's prior-art search results are included in the parent's report. If examiner finds that search results do not cover all divisional claims, a correction order is issued; if deficiencies persist, the expedited-exam request may be rejected; deficiencies addressed (e.g., by submitting additional authorized search report) allow the examiner to decide on expedited examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of prior-art documents in search report (expedited exam)
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, a prior-art search report should include more than five prior-art documents; fewer may be allowed where justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where no close prior art exists compared to the claimed invention or the field is entirely new, the grounds for lacking the required number must be stated and indication of fewer than four documents may be allowed (see referenced paragraph).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search Result contents and format in prior-art search report
rubrics_metrics.description: Search results must set out problems solved in each prior-art document compared with all claims and the means for solving them; indicate relevant pages and lines; list contents related to claimed invention consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search results shall be indicated by searched prior-art document and the claims related to the claimed invention must be indicated in the 'Relevant Claims' box of the search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrastive explanation in prior-art search report
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a claim-by-claim comparison of similarities and differences with the closest prior-art document, indicating prior-art locations in detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: a) Similarities and differences with the closest prior-art document shall be separately described claim-by-claim in detail, indicating concerned pages/lines in the prior art. b) Choose the closest prior-art document for each claim; each claim need not be compared with all prior-art documents. c) In principle provide contrastive explanation for all claims; however, independent claims that differ only in dependent claims/categories may be grouped (more than two claims together). d) If novelty and inventive step are recognized in independent claims (relevance marked 'A'), a brief contrastive explanation for dependent claims may suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling cases where specification amended after commission of prior-art search
rubrics_metrics.description: If a prior-art search was conducted based on pre-amended claims and the specification was amended before filing the expedited request, a re-submitted search report at the time of filing may affect determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where prior-art search was commissioned to an authorized institute, a request for expedited examination is filed after amendment to the claims, and the institute conducted search on pre-amended claims, resubmission of the search report at filing after correction order allows the examiner to make a determination on expedited examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of ground for expedited request due to authorized search after correction order
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ground for the expedited-exam request changes as a result of the authorized prior-art search after a correction order, the applicant must indicate date and name of the institute in corrected documents and the examiner will decide legitimacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds for request can be changed while submitting corrected documents; examiner decides based on legitimacy. Applicant must indicate the date of request for prior-art search and the name of the authorized institute in the corrected document. Examiner may designate the search institution on the system so the prior-art search report can be uploaded. If the written request lacks date/name, the examiner will still undertake the same procedure and designate the search institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for submission of prior-art search report (expedited / super-expedited)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior-art search report for expedited examination must be submitted within one month of the request; for super-expedited, within 10 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior-art search report is not submitted by the time the examiner makes a decision on expedited examination after correction periods elapse, the examiner shall issue another correction order. Failure by the authorized institute to submit within one month triggers correction order procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited examination eligibility for aged or terminally ill applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications filed by persons over 65 or terminally ill patients may be eligible for expedited examination where health may prevent them from taking steps to final disposal of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic requirements: Over 65 is treated as aged. Terminal illness is determined based on diagnosis or doctor's note per Article 3 of the Medical Act; the criterion is whether the applicant's health prevents taking steps in examination procedures (examples of acceptable doctor's notes provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration by examiner prior to appeal (trigger and purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an appellant files a notice of appeal against a decision to reject and submits an amendment within 30 days of the notice, the IPTAB notifies the Commissioner and the examiner shall reexamine the amended application to possibly reverse the rejection and grant a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: protect inventions and reduce appeals by allowing examiners to reexamine amendments submitted within 30 days after filing a notice of appeal. Relevant statutory provisions (Articles 173–175) set procedures and effects (e.g., reversal of rejection if grounds resolved, or reporting results if not).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and time limits for reconsideration before appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Only patent applications subject to a decision to reject (not invalidated/returned) are eligible; appellant must file notice of appeal within 30 days of receiving certified copy of decision to reject; amendment of specification/drawings must be made within 30 days of filing the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment within 30 days is considered formal and is subject to reconsideration even if not substantive. The President of IPTAB can extend the time limit for convenience of remote persons. Notice of appeal must comply with formality requirements (Article 140(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and formality steps for examiner reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of notice of appeal the trial policy division completes formality examination, inputs the case in database, forwards to patent examination bureau, director registers case and assigns to an examiner (preferably the original rejecting examiner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In principle the examiner who made the decision to reject should re-examine; if that examiner moved divisions, another perceived right person shall reexamine. If notice of appeal is defective and the defect was missed and case forwarded, remand to IPTAB is principle unless defect is minor and easily rectified by IPTAB President or presiding judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria for appropriateness of amendments submitted with appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed within 30 days must correspond to those necessitated by final rejection; must be within the scope of originally filed specification/drawings, and claim-scope amendments should be narrowing, clerical corrections, clarifications of ambiguity, or permissible reinstatements per statutory exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (i) amendments must be within the scope of originally filed specification/drawings; (ii) claim-scope amendments count as: 1) narrowing by restriction/deletion/adding an element; 2) clerical error correction; 3) clarifying ambiguous description; 4) amendments beyond scope of paragraph 47(2) to reinstate earlier claims or amend in accordance with listed subparagraphs. If amendments do not satisfy requirements or give rise to new grounds for rejection, the amendment shall be refused entry. Criteria for evaluating requirements and scope refer to Chapter 2 Part 4 of the Examination Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to enter illegitimate amendments and comparison rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment may be refused entry where it does not comply with Article 47(2)-(3) or where new grounds for rejection arise; evaluation of new matter and scope uses comparisons to specific prior versions of the specification/drawings depending on procedural posture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: If previously notified grounds for rejection are not overcome but no new grounds arise, the amendment may be accepted but the original rejection stands. If new grounds arise from the amendment, the amendment shall be refused entry and review proceeds based on the specification prior to amendment. For purposes of assessing introduction of new matter (Article 47(2)), compare with the originally filed specification/drawings; for Article 47(3) requirements compare with the specification/drawings of the immediately prior amendment (amendment II). Whether claim scope is narrowed is determined by comparing corresponding claims between the prior amendment and the new amendment. Several scenarios (amendments I/II/III/IV, refusal to enter, timing of notices) govern which comparison baseline applies.
